ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the stacked diagram above there are five plastic pieces, respectively corresponding to A white triangle, B light-colored square/rectangle, C black circle, D olive-colored long rectangle, and E light-colored pentagon. These shapes in the figure block one another, indicating that they were stacked on in order. Then reason: From the visible blocking relationships, B is more like the bottom-layer piece, and C is above B, but is also partly blocked by the later-placed D and the shapes in front; that is to say, below C there is only one piece placed earlier. According to the rule given in the problem, the piece with only one piece below it is the second piece placed on, so the second piece placed on is C.

method.method_draft: First describe the stack in image1: identify the five pieces matching the options in image2: A is the white triangular piece, B is the pale square/rectangle, C is the black circle, D is the long horizontal olive rectangle, and E is the pale pentagon. Read the visible overlaps in image1: the pale square is partly hidden behind the black circle and behind the horizontal rectangle; the black circle is partly hidden by the horizontal rectangle and by pieces in front; later pieces cover earlier pieces. Build a back-to-front ordering from these occlusions. The piece with exactly one piece underneath it is the second piece placed. This ordering makes C, the black circle, second.
